replies.author: @TrippinWithTim
replies.text: I live in PH and yes, English is everywhere including everything written, signs, menus, contracts. It’s much more western vibe but poor with inferior infrastructure in most areas. There are “bubbles” but at a higher price. I suggest going to both. DaLat is nice cool weather. Like Baguio in Philippines but nicer, better food and more beautiful. DaNang (including Hoi An) are awesome but hot summers, as is most of SE Asia. Nha Trang is terrific and a little less expensive as DaNang rentals and hotels have risen in price. Go to those beach towns Jan-March before the heat gets oppressive. I love spending 90 days in Vietnam and may do that back to back then return to PH home base.

replies.author: @dalexplym4882
replies.text:
You will have language problems in all those countries (including PH); it's just a fact of life -- but you will do OK with a translation app. You can nearly always find an English speaker at hotels, and often at restaurants or other businesses. (Not always on the street, however.) 
My 2 cents: Try VN first. I haven't been to Nicaragua, but it's a small country and there is so much more to see in VN. PH is interesting, but the massive government corruption has made the citizenry lose hope of ever becoming prosperous. The place just carries a heavy vibe, for the most part. VN is growing rapidly, and many young people there are ambitious and optimistic. There is much to do in Saigon, and many lovely places to visit along the coast. I'm going back in a few months.
